its measures, word-structure, Zand, questions and counter-questions, words, and metric feet, and is treated as well-recited and used in worship.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The Gatha Ahunavaiti is associated with its own wisdom, clearness, loving intention, sovereignty, ritual order, and an acquired boon given by Ahura Mazda for piety.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The Ahuna-vairya is worshipped as holy lord of the ritual order with its Ahu and She is allowed to remain in a separate house. Food and drink are placed there; at night Unthlatu enters, consumes them, and leaves. content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.african-nursery-tales-zulus-callaway-archive-l4546-l4653","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zulu/project-gutenberg/nursery-tales-traditions-histories-zulus-callaway.md","passage_locator":{"label":"AMAVUKUTU. / AUAVUKUTU. / USITUNGUSOBENHLE.90 / USITUNGUSOBENHLE.; lines 4546-4653","start":"4546","end":"4653","translation":"Nursery Tales, Traditions, and Histories of the Zulus, in Their Own Words","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"In this excerpt, a cannibal has Usitungusobenthle with him, makes her help find maggots, then places her in his bag and takes her toward her home. Her mother and father also hear her voice. content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.african-nursery-tales-zulus-callaway-archive-l10837-l10982","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zulu/project-gutenberg/nursery-tales-traditions-histories-zulus-callaway.md","passage_locator":{"label":"IZIMU ELA TOLWA UMASENDENI. / UMKXAKAZA WAKOGING QWAYO. / IZINGANEXWANE. / UMKXAK AZ A-WAKOGIN G Q WAY 0.; lines 10837-10982","start":"10837","end":"10982","translation":"Nursery Tales, Traditions, and Histories of the Zulus, in Their Own Words","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Umkxakaza’s mother discovers that her child has been taken by the beast Usilosimapundu, whose cattle had been plundered. Armed men pursue, but their spears fail to wound the beast. The people briefly recover and embrace Umkxakaza, but the beast carries her off again. Her family follows until the father, brother, sister, and finally mother are exhausted. The beast takes Umkxakaza far away to a furnished cave and explains that he has harmed her father in return for the cattle taken from him.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The mother returns home, sees a fence broken down on one side, and asks what has been there.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Ubalatusi says she had been sent by the leaves to fetch water from the river with a vessel and could not get away again.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The mother searches several houses, does not find her child, and tells the men that the child has been taken by the beast whose cattle were plundered.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Armed men follow the tracks of the beast and find it standing still and waiting for them.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The beast laughs and tells the pursuers to do quickly what they are going to do because the sun has set.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The pursuers throw all their spears, but the spears fall into a pool, on a rock, in the grass, and in the forest without stabbing anything; a second arming and attack ends the same way.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The people ask that Umkxakaza be allowed to come down; she descends, and her people kiss her while she and they weep.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The army places Umkxakaza in the middle, but the beast passes through them, she is thrown into the air, and the beast goes away with her.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The mother, father, brother, and sister follow the beast and rest when it rests; the father, brother, and sister become tired and turn back.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The beast gives sugarcane and maize to Umkxakaza’s mother, and she eats.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"When the mother becomes tired, she asks the beast to let Umkxakaza come down so she can see her; mother and daughter weep, kiss, and the mother tells her child to go in peace.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"The beast takes Umkxakaza far away to a place
